arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Fleming argued that the government agrees the statutory bar does not block review of the agency's threshold determination of ineligibility.
Mr. Raynor argued that the statute precludes review of any judgment regarding the granting of relief under specific provisions.
Ms. Meehan argued that an alternative meaning of judgment still bars review in this specific case.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of a statutory bar on judicial review. The bar targets decisions regarding the granting of relief. The core question is whether this bar covers the agency's threshold finding that an immigrant is ineligible for status adjustment.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundary of judicial oversight over immigration agency decisions. It determines whether courts can correct errors in the initial eligibility screening process. The outcome shapes the balance between agency discretion and individual rights in immigration law.
